title: Aussie workers’ list of demands
full_text:
Flexible work has gone from a standout perk to a bare minimum, with Australians now demanding their employers fund health insurance and hand them back Fridays as cost-of-living pressures fundamentally change what employees expect from the workplace.
Research from comparison site iSelect found that while 54 per cent of workers still wanted flexible arrangements, nearly half – 48 per cent – were demanding a four-day work week, and 45 per cent wanted their employer to foot the bill for private health insurance.
Free meals and snacks ranked fourth among demands at 35 per cent, followed by professional development opportunities at 31 per cent.
iSelect comparison expert Sophie Ryan said workers were becoming increasingly deliberate about evaluating the total value of an employment package, not just their salary.
“Flexibility is no longer viewed as a temporary post-pandemic perk – many Aussies are seeing it as a fundamental part of achieving better work-life balance, managing caring responsibilities and reducing commuting costs and time,” she said.
Ms Ryan said the strong appetite for employer-paid health cover was particularly significant, as many workers now viewed private health insurance as a practical financial benefit rather than a workplace luxury.
“Private health cover may provide access to greater choice in healthcare, support services that Medicare may not cover and, in some cases, help people access treatment sooner through the private healthcare system,” she said.
The revelation comes as many Australian workplaces continue to grapple with getting staff back to the office, for even a few days a week.
The four-day work week result signals that time is increasingly being valued on par with money. Ms Ryan noted that for many workers, an extra day away from the office carried the same weight as a direct financial benefit – pointing to growing concerns around burnout and mental health.
